utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-A, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. I would like to begin by ensuring that the audio equipment is working properly. Can the appellants hear the proceedings in a language they understand, beginning with Mr. Prlic? Can you hear me? THE APPELLANT PRLIC: Could you repeat the question because I was dealing with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, you have answered my question now. You understand, too? THE APPELLANT PRLIC: I didn't hear because I was dealing with something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes. You can understand the proceedings? THE APPELLANT PRLIC: Yeah, I understand you. I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You can be seated. Mr. Stojic. THE APPELLANT STOJIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Everything is okay. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I can hear you very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Petkovic. THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you well. I can understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petkovic. Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Everything is in order. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Pusic. THE APPELLANT PUSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Prosecution, I suppose you can hear and understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Mr. President, we do. And for the record it's Douglas Stringer, Sarah Finnin, and Case Manager Janet Stewart appearing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. Defence, for Mr. Prlic, I understand that Mr. Karnavas is participating via video-conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] That's correct, Your Honour, and I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, that's reassuring. I was worried about that. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. For Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Senka Nozica representing Mr. Stojic and Aidan Alice [phoen] my legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nozica. For Mr. Petkovic now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. Currently in the courtroom only Vesna Alaburic representing General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Alaburic. For Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, co-counsel Drazen Plavec representing Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plavec. For Mr. Pusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Today representing Mr. Pusic, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic and Mulalic, Nermin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand Mr. Praljak will represent himself? THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, Slobodan Praljak is representing Slobodan Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. Thank you all. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. In the present case the last Status Conference was held on 3 February 2014. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by order filed on 14 May 2014. Let me now turn to inquiring into the status of the detention conditions and health situation of the appellants. If any of the appellants wishes, I can have this discussion take place in closed session. Is there any request for closing this session? I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you know that the correspondence between the Trial Chamber and Mr. Pusic was confidential, so if Mr. Pusic wants to say something about that I would kindly ask you to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So it will depend on whether such a request is made by Mr. Pusic and so far it has not been made. If it is made, there is no problem, I will close the session. Update of the case. I recall the Notices of Appeal of Mr. Praljak and Pusic which were filed on 28 June 2013. I recall that the Notice of Appeal of the Prosecution was filed on 27 August 2013. On 21 June 2013 upon request of the parties I ordered that the Notices of Appeal of Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, and Mr. Coric be filed within 60 days of the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement. I further recall that I ordered Mr. Praljak, Mr. Pusic, and the Prosecution to file their appeal briefs no later than 135 days from the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement and that, as a result, there is a harmonised briefing scheduled in place for all the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I note that since the last Status Conference the Appeals Chamber has issued a number of decisions on pre-appeal motions. In particular, on 6 March 2014, the Appeals Chamber issued its decision on Prosecution motion for order striking grounds from Berislav Pusic's Notices of Appeal and on Berislav Pusic's application for leave to file a corrigendum to his Notice of Appeal, in which the Appeals Chamber ordered Mr. Pusic to re-file his Notice of Appeal in accordance with the requirements set out in the relevant provisions of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the practice direction on formal requirements for appeal from judgement. On 4 April 2014, the Appeals Chamber issued its decision on Praljak's motions for stay of procedure and assignment of counsel in the interest of justice, in which the Appeals Chamber denied both of Mr. Praljak's motions. On 13 May 2014, the Appeals Chamber issued its order on the Registrar's application pursuant to Rule 45(E) of the Rules, ordering Mr. Praljak to reimburse to the Tribunal for the costs sustained in providing Mr. Praljak with legal aid. On 21 May 2014, in my capacity as pre-Appeals Judge in this case, I issued, one, an order lifting the confidential and ex parte status of a letter sent to me on 28 April 2014, by which Mr. Slobodan Praljak informed me of his decision to represent himself in these proceedings and the requested translations of all filed documents in Croatian and a stay of proceedings until translations are received; and two, a decision allowing Mr. Prlic's counsel to participate in this Status Conference via video-conference. Let me now turn to the parties and ask whether they have any issues that they would like to raise. You would like to?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to raise an issue that interests most of us all and that is whether we can receive any information with regard to the date when we could be provided with the translation of the judgement into English. I would like to emphasise that my client is very interested in that translation to coincide with the B/C/S translation of the judgement because pursuant to the Rules of the Tribunal he has to be able to participate actively in his appeal and the drafting of his appeal. If you have any sort of information, I would kindly ask you to impart that information that concerns all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I would like to give you some information, tentative as it will be, to give you an idea where we stand. We are now anticipating that the English translation of the judgement would be available sometime in June, so quite soon now. As regards the B/C/S translation, we expect it to be available in September. This gives you, Mrs. Nozica, some idea and I hope that this is helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, this is very helpful. We would kindly ask you if there is any possibility for the translation into B/C/S to come a bit closer to the translation into English, that would be very useful for our clients because the three-month difference is a big difference and it will affect the preparation of our appeal, in view of the time that we have been given to prepare it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please pass on to the language services the comment just made by Mrs. Nozica. These are -- insofar as the Defence is concerned, these are the comments I suppose? I don't see anything else. The Prosecutor -- THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm terribly sorry. Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to hand in a piece of paper for Your Honour. Maybe I may be allowed to give it to the officer, who can then hand it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: What is this paper about? THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] These are my objections to some conclusions in the appeals judgement, and if you wish me to do so I can actually list some of those facts. For example, on two occasions it is stated that I requested a breakdown of the costs that the Registry, i.e., the Court, had in terms of the payment of my Defence. At the last Status Conference I said that I did not request that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I think that the more proper procedure would be if you have some comments in writing, is to present them in the proper form, and I presume that this is something that would be shared with the Prosecution. This is not ex parte, is it? But in any event, I think that done in a proper form of a motion or whatever it is would be something that could be -- I would favour. Handing in a piece of paper to the President, to the pre-Appeal Judge or Presiding Judge is perhaps -- in this form is not -- THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You can of course file your form for the record, but I would like to follow a more formal procedure, whether by motion or filing with the Court for the record. So I suggest that you follow one of those procedures and that we do not proceed to discuss those objections of yours now orally. If that's agreeable with you, I will now turn to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to inform Your Honour that probably shortly after today's proceedings, possibly tomorrow morning, the Prosecution will be filing its response in regard to the letter of General Praljak that was recently made available to us on the issue of representation and the other matters that are raised in the letter. So Your Honour will have that probably later today or by tomorrow after its distributed by the Registry. And secondly, just to confirm for the record, Mr. President, that now that in view of Your Honour's decision on the issue of funding and representation for Mr. Praljak, the Prosecution is going now to start making its disclosure directly to General Praljak and we're going to follow the procedures that have been followed in other cases on appeal where the accused was self-representing, Krajisnik and I think Tolimir, in which we made our disclosures through the Registry. And so I just wanted to put that on the record and to inform General Praljak that as we continue to make our document reviews and disclosure, we will be working with Registry to provide those materials directly to him since he no longer has counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I suppose this is agreeable to Mr. Praljak? THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. Any additional issues for the Prosecution? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So as the appellants do not have any other issues they would like to raise, I would like to thank the parties for their attendance -- THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I spoke too soon I see. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] No, I would just like to respond. Obviously I will receive documents as per procedure, but I will receive only those in Croatian or the B/C/S language as they call it here. These are the only documents I am prepared to receive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Comments, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it raises an issue that goes right to the heart of the matter. Certainly when I'm talking about disclosure now, we're basically talking about disclosure of things that -- of relevance to the case that have come in in the meantime from other trials and what not, and generally these tend to be documents from the region. And so generally the original language is B/C/S, and so with respect to probably most of what I'm referring to now as disclosure, there won't be an issue because the original language is B/C/S. Also, of course with other documents, it's very likely that we will have a translation into B/C/S if it's already in English or a different language. So I don't see a problem there. Of course, the longer-term problem, as Your Honour knows, relates to some of the items that Mr. Praljak's requesting, such as trial transcripts and final trial briefs and all the rest. And we've made a reference to that issue in the submission that we're going to be submitting later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will look at it when we receive it. So I would like now to thank the parties for their participation and to call these proceedings to a close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.51 p.m. 24 25
